body.en: Jacob and Monod described the lac operon of E. coli. The regulatory gene i codes for the repressor. Three structural genes follow the operator: z (β-galactosidase, which breaks lactose into glucose and galactose), y (permease, which lets lactose in) and a (transacetylase). Without lactose the repressor binds the operator and stops RNA polymerase from transcribing the operon. When lactose (the inducer) enters, it binds the repressor and inactivates it, so the genes are transcribed. Because the repressor switches it off, this is negative regulation.
body.kn: ಜಾಕೊಬ್ ಮತ್ತು ಮೊನೊಡ್ lac ಒಪೆರಾನ್ ವಿವರಿಸಿದರು. i ಜೀನ್ ದಮನಕಾರಿಯನ್ನು ಸಂಕೇತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; z, y, a ರಚನಾತ್ಮಕ ಜೀನ್‌ಗಳು. ಲ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೋಸ್ ಪ್ರೇರಕವಾಗಿ ದಮನಕಾರಿಯನ್ನು ನಿಷ್ಕ್ರಿಯಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಇದು ಋಣಾತ್ಮಕ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ.

title.en: Board: the lac operon, the genome and DNA fingerprints

say.en: The lac operon: the regulator gene i makes the repressor; then come the promoter, the operator, and the structural genes z, y and a.
With no lactose, the repressor sits on the operator and blocks RNA polymerase: the operon is off.

text.en: No lactose: repressor on o → OFF

say.en: Lactose, the inducer, binds the repressor and inactivates it; the genes are transcribed. Because a repressor controls it, this is negative regulation.
The Human Genome Project, 1990 to 2003: about 3164.7 million bases and about 30,000 genes, with less than 2 percent coding for proteins.
DNA fingerprinting compares repeated DNA, VNTRs. Fragments are separated on a gel; matching band patterns point to the same person.

narration.en: Start with no lactose: the operon stays off. Add lactose and press play. Watch the repressor let go, RNA polymerase run along the genes, and the operon switch off again once the lactose is used up.

caption.en: Without lactose the repressor (made by gene i) binds the operator and blocks RNA polymerase. Lactose, the inducer, binds the repressor and inactivates it, so z, y and a are transcribed and the enzymes are made. As β-galactosidase uses up the lactose, the repressor binds again: negative regulation. Numbers are schematic.
caption.kn: ಲ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೋಸ್ ಇಲ್ಲದಿದ್ದರೆ ದಮನಕ ಆಪರೇಟರ್‌ಗೆ ಅಂಟಿ RNA ಪಾಲಿಮರೇಸ್ ತಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಪ್ರಚೋದಕ ಲ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೋಸ್ ದಮನಕವನ್ನು ನಿಷ್ಕ್ರಿಯಗೊಳಿಸಿದಾಗ z, y, a ಪ್ರತಿಲೇಖನಗೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತವೆ. ಲ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೋಸ್ ಮುಗಿದಂತೆ ದಮನಕ ಮತ್ತೆ ಅಂಟುತ್ತದೆ: ಋಣಾತ್ಮಕ ನಿಯಂತ್ರಣ.

title.en: Human Genome Project and DNA fingerprinting

body.en: The Human Genome Project ran from 1990 to 2003. The human genome has about 3164.7 million bases; the average gene has 3000 bases, and the largest, dystrophin, has 2.4 million. There are about 30,000 genes; less than 2% of the genome codes for proteins; 99.9% of bases are the same in all people; chromosome 1 has the most genes (2968) and Y the fewest (231); about 1.4 million single-base differences (SNPs) were found. DNA fingerprinting, developed by Alec Jeffreys, compares repetitive DNA, especially satellite DNA with variable number tandem repeats (VNTRs). DNA is digested, separated by electrophoresis, blotted and hybridised with a labelled VNTR probe (Southern blotting). It is used in forensics and paternity testing.
body.kn: ಮಾನವ ಜೀನೋಮ್ ಯೋಜನೆ 1990–2003. ಸುಮಾರು 30,000 ಜೀನ್‌ಗಳು; 2%ಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಭಾಗ ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್ ಸಂಕೇತಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; 99.9% ಕ್ಷಾರಗಳು ಎಲ್ಲರಲ್ಲೂ ಒಂದೇ. ಅಲೆಕ್ ಜೆಫ್ರೀಸ್ ಅಭಿವೃದ್ಧಿಪಡಿಸಿದ DNA ಬೆರಳಚ್ಚು VNTRಗಳನ್ನು ಹೋಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: Predict whether the lac genes are transcribed in E. coli cells (a) grown in glucose without lactose, (b) given lactose, (c) given lactose but carrying a mutant repressor that cannot bind the inducer.

steps.en: (a) No lactose, so the active repressor sits on the operator: genes are off.
(b) Lactose binds and inactivates the repressor: genes are on.
(c) The repressor cannot be inactivated, so it stays on the operator: genes stay off.
